# Private SOURCE_ONLY event-bound probe (v2, not for promotion)

The4093-byte C39 profile admits owner4 and exact C20 INLINE_CONT1 before phase
access. It keeps the actual source/AUTH13/typed graph, CR own/page CRC and schema
checks. Once that CR is authenticated, only an actual event count of0..8 may
continue to INLINE page reads; larger counts end this owned query and hand off
to C26 SOURCE_FALLBACK5. Existing validator rejects counts>=65536 as corrupt.
Success ends its reader and requests20/1/A1. This SOURCE_ONLY profile has no
ordinary caller A0/A2 publication path. Cancellation/errors do not resume C20.
It introduces no new state, object, bank or resident code.

The actual45-case SOURCE matrix passes independent geometry/maps, continuation
backup, canonical/history/shim and full16MiB guards, plus64 exact admission
predicate cases. Actual SOURCE_ONLY entry tests cover six foreign owners/all
ops, invalid continuation tags before phase, and COUNT0 (unchanged styles/roles,
all21 hidden-mask bytes cleared, no lease,20/1 handoff). Resealed actual typed
CR/page count faults9..65535 decline before INL reads;0/high24-bit counts reject
C2 and a false8-count short stream rejects the existing C0 fault. No failed
result resumes C20 or publishes consumable output. This is manual actual
REQUEST/OP dispatch, not a registered/resident/native integration claim.

The optional C26 gate remains3327 bytes when disabled and3436 when enabled;
C20 is byte-identical. See the immutable adaptive-source profile for that gate.
`tests/test_cache_inline_event_bound.py` builds and runs this profile.

Performance remains insufficient with the512-byte admission threshold. BODY512
with4/8 events regresses16.5%/38.1%; BODY1024 with8 regresses8.3%. Sparse998B
improves23.2%, and a66004B body improves97.9%. Dense1800B/300events now safely
falls back after two C39 calls (7.3% overhead), instead of v1's6.19x cost. This
profile is preserved as a rejected threshold experiment. The next v3 should
raise admission to4096 bytes and remeasure sparse/dense/packed-page costs.
